boards.title: Your First Weekend at Miami University-Oxford, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe, evergreen first-weekend sequence that moves from campus orientation to shared activities, quiet exploration, and Oxford’s outdoor spaces.

cards.title: Start at the Armstrong Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday: 550 E. Spring St., Oxford
cards.notes: Use the student center as a first meeting point: check its event calendar, find a lounge or study space, and make a plan with the people you meet.
cards.short_summary: A central campus gathering place with student spaces, services, dining, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes Armstrong as its college union, with meeting rooms, quiet study spaces, lounge space, student-organization offices, dining, and major event spaces.
cards.access_notes: Fall 2026 building hours listed by Miami are 7 a.m.–midnight weekdays and 9 a.m.–midnight weekends, with listed holiday exceptions.

cards.title: Break the ice in the Red Zone
cards.subtitle: Friday: Armstrong Student Center
cards.notes: Bring a few new acquaintances to the Red Zone for a low-pressure game of billiards, foosball, air hockey, cards, or a board game.
cards.short_summary: A named Armstrong game room built for casual group activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami lists 12 TVs, a karaoke machine, board games, billiards, foosball, and air hockey in the Red Zone Game Room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Armstrong Student Center; check the center’s current building hours and any event reservations before going.

cards.title: Get oriented at King Library
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning: Oxford campus
cards.notes: Walk through the library early in the weekend and identify a future work spot, the Makerspace, Sidley Lounge, and Howe Writing Center.
cards.short_summary: Miami’s flagship library and a practical anchor for academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami Libraries calls King Library its flagship and notes the Makerspace, Sidley Lounge, and Howe Writing Center as popular venues.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current library access and hours through Miami University Libraries before visiting.

cards.title: See fossils and meteorites at Limper
cards.subtitle: Saturday: Shideler Hall, Room 126
cards.notes: Add a short self-guided museum stop between campus walks; look closely at the local fossils, mineral specimens, rocks, and meteorites on display.
cards.short_summary: A compact geology museum with local fossils and global specimens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Limper Geology Museum in Shideler Hall displays fossils, minerals, rocks, and meteorites and is free and open to visitors of all ages.
cards.access_notes: Miami lists hours Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; the museum is beside Shideler Hall’s first-floor lobby.

cards.title: Visit the Hefner Museum’s Imaginarium
cards.subtitle: Saturday: Upham Hall
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum visit and spend time with the Imaginarium’s hands-on natural-history displays, including its “Bugs Rule the World” exhibit.
cards.short_summary: A public natural-history museum with a renovated interactive area.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami states that the Hefner Museum is open to the public Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., and that its renovated Imaginarium includes “Bugs Rule the World.”
cards.source_title: Visit the Museum | Hefner Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Miami lists public hours of 9 a.m.–4 p.m. Monday–Friday and notes that the museum closes on university holidays.

cards.entity_name: Richard and Carole Cocks Art Museum Sculpture Park
cards.title: Walk the Cocks Art Museum Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon: 801 S. Patterson Ave.
cards.notes: Make the sculpture grounds a daylight walk: view the outdoor works and use the visit to learn where the museum will reopen after renovations.
cards.short_summary: Year-round outdoor sculpture grounds beside Miami’s art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami states that the museum’s sculpture park is open year-round while its galleries are closed for renovation through Fall 2027.
cards.source_title: Richard and Carole Cocks Art Museum
cards.access_notes: The galleries are closed for renovations through Fall 2027; Miami identifies the Sculpture Park as open year-round.

cards.entity_name: Public skating at Goggin Ice Center
cards.title: Check a public-skating session at Goggin
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening: 610 S. Oak St.
cards.notes: Look up the current public-skate schedule, register if required, and invite a small group for an activity that does not depend on a campus organization.
cards.short_summary: An ice-center activity at Miami’s two-rink recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami lists public skating among Goggin Ice Center’s recreational opportunities and provides a public-skate registration link.
cards.access_notes: Public-skate availability is schedule-dependent; use Goggin’s current facility schedule and registration information before heading over.

cards.entity_name: Climbing Center at the Recreational Sports Center
cards.title: Try the Climbing Center
cards.subtitle: Sunday: Recreational Sports Center, 750 S. Oak St.
cards.notes: If you have facility access, check the Climbing Center’s current schedule and try the bouldering cave or ask about an introductory climbing option.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation climbing space with beginner and ongoing programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami says its Climbing Center offers equipment rentals, Climbing Fundamentals, a Lead Series class, and a free bouldering cave.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and climbing activities may have separate requirements; verify current facility hours and program details with Miami Recreation.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk at Silvoor
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon: 910 Silvoor Lane, Oxford
cards.notes: Choose a daylight walk and stay on the route; use the sanctuary’s trail information to notice the wildflower garden and the changing seasonal landscape.
cards.short_summary: A named natural-area sanctuary with a wildflower garden and trail access.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami describes Silvoor Biological Sanctuary as a 2.5-acre tract with an extensive wildflower garden and gives its entrance as 910 Silvoor Lane.
cards.source_title: Places to Visit | Miami University Natural Areas
cards.access_notes: Use the official trail map and visit in daylight; the Natural Areas prohibit fires, hunting, bicycling, and camping.

cards.title: Look for a game or performance at Millett Hall
cards.subtitle: Weekend closer: 500 E. Sycamore St.
cards.notes: Check Miami’s current calendar for an all-ages game, assembly, or performance, then use the building as a recognizable campus landmark on your route.
cards.short_summary: A large campus arena used for RedHawk basketball and university performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Miami identifies Millett Hall as the home of Miami RedHawk basketball and a site for university assemblies and performances.
cards.source_title: Visit Us | Miami University Performing Arts Series
cards.access_notes: Attendance and admission depend on the specific scheduled event; confirm event details, ticketing, and parking before visiting.
